title: Online privacy kindness and help
outcome: Stay safe online; recognise risks and my digital footprint (Safer Internet Day).
credit: Lesson resource · CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: free for classroom use, share and adapt with credit, no resale
step_out: Before teaching, agree a discreet pause signal and an available adult. Staff acknowledge the signal quietly and support the familiar supervised quiet route. No public explanation is needed. Offer a neutral task, supported return or private catch-up; do not send a learner away alone.
safeguarding: Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe, investigate or promise secrecy. Record concerns through the safeguarding route, separately from learning evidence. Follow the immediate school route for urgent concerns. A pupil unable to identify a trusted adult is supported privately, not pressed.
help_route: Stop engaging with a concerning message or post and tell a trusted adult or school staff privately. Ask for help with report or block tools; do not forward private or unkind content. If the first adult is unavailable or help is insufficient, ask another trusted adult. Staff can help find an appropriate helpline by type if needed, without naming a service in the lesson.
privacy: The personal online-safety pledge stays with the learner. Do not collect, photograph, display or compare it. Use an invented learner, leave it blank or pass without a reason. No personal account details, names, passwords, locations, contact information or experiences are requested.
marking: Retain actual fictional learning evidence, normal access and content prompts. Give one next step and allow the learner's own response in their usual mode. E only for actual banked evidence; R only after Voice, Audience, a next step and an actual pupil response. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm any mapping. Never infer online safety from a pledge or collect private concerns in learning records.

scenarios.A: A young person drafts a photo of a card model. A note in the back shows their routine. Another learner is in the photo. The young person has not asked to share it.
scenarios.B: A young person wants to share a photo of a card tower. Another learner is in the photo and has not agreed. An unkind reply appears in the draft group chat. No unkind words are shown.
scenarios.C: A young person drafts a group note. It shows details of their routine. A second draft reply is unkind. No unkind words are shown. They want a safer way to join in.
scenarios.model: The learner can remove the routine details and not post the other learner without asking. A private setting can limit who sees a post, but people may copy it. Kind words can stay about the card model. If a reply causes concern, they can stop replying and ask a trusted adult in private for help to report or block it.

hinge.question: A private setting means a photo can be shared without asking. Which response is best?
choices: A Share it since it is private.
B Check details and ask first. Copies may still be made.
C Send it to more people to check.
D Delete the account so all copies vanish.
hinge.parallel: An unkind reply appears. A Stop replying and ask a trusted adult for help with report or block tools. B Send it on to more people.

paragraphs: Stay safe online; recognise risks and my digital footprint (Safer Internet Day).
All cases are invented and offline. Accept other safe, reasoned answers. No personal accounts are needed.
A choice about who can see personal information. Share less and check who can see it.
The trace from things a person does or shares online. Other people may copy or share a post. Deleting it may not remove all copies.
Clear permission. Ask before sharing a photo or details about another person. If they do not agree, do not post it.
Use respectful words. Do not join in, forward or add to an unkind reply. A person can get help without replying.
Tools that can flag a problem or limit contact. A trusted adult can help use them. Help is still valid if tools are unclear or do not work.

Keep routine details private. In A, a routine note and another learner in the photo create risks. Remove the detail and do not post the other learner without consent. Kind comments can stay about the work. Settings can limit viewers; they cannot guarantee control of copies. Do not imply consent solves every privacy risk.

Match removing routine details to sharing less personal information. Improve Private means no one can copy it: settings can limit an audience, but copies may still be made. The learner should think before posting and ask an adult if unsure.

Main B. A confuses settings with consent. C spreads the content. D claims deletion removes all copies. If unclear, re-model A and repeat privately. Parallel A: stop replying and get trusted adult help with report or block tools. A pass is unobserved.

Risk: another learner has not agreed to be in a shared photo. An unkind reply could spread if joined in or sent on. Do not post that photo without consent; use a version with no other person or private details instead. Copies may remain once shared. Use kind words about the card tower. Stop replying to a concerning message and ask a trusted adult in private for help to report or block it. This reduces further sharing and gets adult support.

A possible note: Leave the routine details out of the group note. A post can be copied, which adds to a digital footprint. Use kind words and do not join in or send on the unkind reply. If it causes concern, stop replying and ask school staff in private for help with report or block tools. This keeps more details private and helps limit the spread. Accept a shorter response with all checks in the pupil usual mode.

Both choices spot a risk, explain a footprint or copy limit, and give a kind safer step with a reason and private help. A map needs no art skill; a note needs no extra words. Reading, typing, aids and an exact scribe do not supply the pupil thinking. Log adult content prompts.
Choose either task. Read one part at a time. Keep the word bank, A model and starters. Offer two safe steps if needed. Record adult answer cues apart from usual access.
Choose either task. Spot a risk, explain copies and the footprint, give a kind safer step with a reason, and add private help. Normal aids and the visible model stay.
Choose either task. Explain a limit of a setting or deletion. Adapt the response if the first adult is busy or a report tool is unclear. No extra disclosure or public talk.

Improve Just delete it and it is gone: copies may remain, so get adult help and do not send it on. Exit can explain a safer step from a story or correct the privacy myth. Do not grade a personal pledge or ask pupils to prove settings on an account.

Judge story risk knowledge and the safe response apart. Secure work links a case risk, footprint or copy limit, a kind feasible step and its reason, and a help route. Keep partial work. Silence or pass is unobserved. No claim that this lesson proves safe habits or stops harm.

Books are the first route. Type instead on Evidence Sheet page 2 works for either choice. Point, draw, use an aid or use an exact scribe. Read back quietly and allow correction. Keep usual reading and language aids. Plan in any language. No public questioning.

The pledge is private and stays with the learner. Do not collect, photograph, display or compare it. Use a fictional pledge, leave it blank or pass. No names, account details or personal story are needed. A pledge is not a safety guarantee. Do not blame a pupil if harm occurs. A fictional pledge can show the same learning.

Retain first thinking, one next step and the learner reply in their own colour or usual mode. Total 40 minutes. Short quiet pauses and processing time sit inside these phases. Choices B and C share one 12 minute work period; do not teach both as extra tasks.

Correct B: check details and ask first; copies may still be made. A confuses private with permission. C spreads the content further. D wrongly promises deletion removes all copies. Ask for one reason privately. If unclear, re-model A, then use the parallel check.
